_rule: Describe what THAT camera can see, and omit what it cannot. Palette and material words are IDENTITY and are byte-identical across all eight; only anatomy and framing words change. A rear camera is never told about a beard, a face, or the belt medallion — E01 measured that a shared prompt asking for 'a long red beard, gold necklace' on every view put a face on the back of the head at both 0.92 and 0.75 denoise, and that per-view prompting alone took face detections 1 -> 0 with silhouette held at IoU 0.784.
_orientation: Measured, not assumed: the sword tip sits at std-frame X -0.150, Y -0.156, so the greatsword is held FORWARD and on the character's RIGHT. Camera yaw N here equals turn_render view yaw N. yaw 90 = camera at +X = his LEFT flank (sword on the far side). yaw 270 = camera at -X = his RIGHT flank (sword side, nearest camera). yaw 45/315 = front three-quarters (315 is the sword side, and the blade crosses frame centre). yaw 135/225 = back three-quarters. el +55 = camera 55 deg above, so the crown and the tops of the pauldrons dominate and the face is strongly foreshortened.
_palette_spine: dark green ribbed knitted sleeveless tunic, ornate polished gold pauldrons, dark wine-red layered cloth skirt, plain wide dark brown leather belt band, gold-trimmed brown leather bracers, gold knee plates, heavy dark charcoal boots, plain flat grey background, painterly visible brushstrokes, worked matte surface
_order_why: Director ruling at Gate 0. The brush runs at denoise 1.0 inside the mask and a hole texel has no content to preserve, so the model composes freely and anchors only on the prompt and the contour. Stroke order therefore controls how much anchoring context each camera gets. The first ordering opened on yaw 90, which is 95% hole and the furthest camera from both styled poles — the single worst-anchored view in the set — and it returned three inventions: a plaited belt, a strap across the upper arm, and a green tunic extended to mid-thigh. The strokes now spiral OUTWARD from the styled front and back poles: at 45 deg roughly half the visible surface already carries projected twin paint, so the brush extends an existing character instead of composing one, and each commit hands more context to the next stroke. The flanks come up late, anchored on both sides.
_negative: braided belt, plaited belt, woven belt, rope belt, shoulder strap, chest strap, baldric, bandolier, watermark, text, logo, blurry, photo, deformed
_negative_why: Held byte-identical across all eight, like the palette words, so per-view POSITIVE prompting stays the only variable — the form E01 actually measured. The first seven terms are Director-named failures observed at Gate 0, not speculation. Paired change in _palette_spine: 'plain wide dark brown leather belt band' became 'plain wide dark brown leather belt band', because the phrase 'wrapped straps' is a plausible seed for BOTH the braid and the arm strap, and negating a term the positive prompt is still asking for is a weaker fix than not asking for it.
